start.values.hint: The variables declared by the ticked scripts and by your script are listed here. Values are strings. An optional field left empty is not sent, and the script reads undefined. If a required field is empty, capture-ledger names it in a 400.
start.ua.compatible: Put in the pattern without Headless
start.ua.hint: '{'chrome'}' is replaced with the browser's own string (without Headless). If it contains the word BrowserHive, robots.txt is read by the rules for that name.
start.schedule.name: Name
start.schedule.hint: Makes a schedule from what the form holds now. Times are read in Asia/Tokyo. The result appears in the schedules view.
start.inline.hint: It is type-checked as strict TypeScript (the first level's compile step). Wrap it in an IIFE, give elements a type and use ?.. For bundled JS, tick "Skip the type check" (it puts // @ts-nocheck on line 1). Write import '{' z '}' from "zod" as the first statement to use Zod (not available with "Before navigation"). A variable declared with const '{' query '}' = defineParams(z.object('{' … '}')) gets a field under "Per-crawl values". export cannot be written (compile stops it with BH0006: in a page it is a syntax error, and nothing would run). Your script runs in the order of the numbers of the scripts with "After load" (first, to begin with), and before everything else with "Before navigation". The name of the script (after inline-) starts with a lowercase letter and holds lowercase letters, digits and -, up to 57 characters. The name with inline- in front becomes the id of this script.
